name: hyp
description: Hyp Machine — hypothesis-driven development for Claude Code. Write an idea as a hypothesis with pass-or-fail checks declared up front; the plugin runs the experiment and records keep, discard, or refine. Outcomes land in a shared, append-only corpus your team and its agents build on: write-once capture, an indexed wiki layer, a compiled dashboard, decision cards, and an explicit operating model — profile-gated so you adopt only what you need. Commands use the /hyp: prefix. Lineage: 0.1.0 is the crux plugin's 0.4.0 feature state, renamed 2026-08-29. 0.2.0 adds work-graph dispatch and session durability: ranked next-item dispatch at session boundaries, claim TTL takeover, K-strikes quarantine, reboot-surviving resume, compression-surviving re-hydration protocol. 0.3.0 adds the flow-governance layer: a rules registry with compiled laws and expiry lint, rule-retest decisions, a license-join guard on rule writes, the flow-leak meter, and the reflex slowdown sensor with a required install self-test — plus dispatch REFILL from licensed follow-up lanes, model-compiled orchestration ratified by its lab keep, and the hardened crux migration formalized in a tagged release. The destination-map program (lab H-DRAFT-2cae0933) adds north-star files whose conditions derive their status from committed verdicts (never stored, never edited), single-file run checkpoints compiled from graded run bytes with typed refusals, the compiled progress view with frontier and distance, and the hypothesis-verdict closes-when predicate.
